$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under src/ imports this file.
purpose: The guard ledger for WIN-258 TRANCHE 5 — `secrets`' canonical store, the
SIXTH owner behind the one PostgreSQL client ADR M0.3 §15 gives the ORM, and
the first whose ports could not be spread into `PostgresTenancyAdapter` at
all. One entry per guard: per scope predicate, per clause the port's own
contract says must be re-checked inside a statement, per lock, per shape
check that stands where a migration-only CHECK stands, and per closed union
a row is read back through. Each carries the file it lives in, the EXACT
text that implements it (`from`), the edit that removes it (`to`), and the
NAMED cases that were seen to go red (`kills`).
IT IS A SIXTH FILE beside mutations.json, mutations-identity.json,
mutations-ports.json, mutations-outbox.json, mutations-tools.json,
mutations-agents.json and mutations-cost.json rather than an extension of
any of them, for the reason the others are separate: each tranche is a
separate claim about a separate port surface, and a reader checking one
should not have to read past the rest. All are hashed by the same
packages.adapters.config rule and counted together by the v1 ledger.
WHY THIS TRANCHE NEEDED ITS OWN SWEEP. Three of the four rows are effectively
IMMUTABLE — the database freezes four columns on `Credential`, nine on
`CredentialSecretVersion`, and refuses UPDATE, DELETE and TRUNCATE outright
on `CredentialAudit` with the privileges revoked from PUBLIC on top — so a
defect written into any of them cannot be corrected afterwards. And the
port's hardest promises are all about what does NOT happen: a purge must
re-check every eligibility clause INSIDE its delete (a read-then-delete loses
the race and raises 23503 mid-batch), `loadForUpdate` must take a lock two
rotations serialise on (a lock nothing can be observed blocking on is
decorative), and a revoked credential must leave the find path while staying
in the inventory. None of that is visible in a returned value on a store with
one caller, which is exactly the shape of guard a green suite hides.
ONE ENTRY MAKES A GUARD STRICTER RATHER THAN LOOSER, AND IT IS DELIBERATE.
M-S45 gives `requireAuditOrdinal` the positivity rule its envelope sibling
has. `CredentialAudit` carries no `> 0` CHECK, so the mutated guard refuses a
row PostgreSQL accepts — the drift that would only ever show up in production
as a refusal nobody could explain, and the one direction a constraints suite
written only as 'the guard refuses what the CHECK refuses' cannot see.
procedure: PROVE THE SUITES GREEN FIRST. Tranche 1's first sweep reported 22 kills and
every one was VACUOUS: a context's `dist` had been cleaned, so every suite
failed to load its import and would have 'died' against any mutation at all,
including none. The driver runs each suite set UNMUTATED and refuses to sweep
unless it is green with a non-zero executed case count, and classifies a run
with no executed cases as VACUOUS rather than as a kill.
THE EIGHTH SUITE IS THIS SWEEP'S RESULT, exactly as `cost-idempotency` was
one store over. Six clauses had no named case anywhere in the tree — the
environment clause on the row lock, the total order under a non-unique query,
`FOR UPDATE OF version`, the retention window, the cutoff re-check inside the
delete, and the candidate list's own copy of the window. Each was falsifiable
only through a transcript that happened to differ, or not at all.
`secrets-scope.integration.test.ts` is five named cases for them.
EACH ENTRY NAMES THE SUITE FILES IT IS SWEPT AGAINST, and the driver runs
only those. A mutation swept against the whole set would be slower and would
also hide the fact that a guard's only witness is a file nobody would think
to look in — which is the fact the `suites` list is here to record.
THE ADAPTER'S OWN SOURCE NEEDS NO REBUILD between edits: vitest transpiles
`packages/adapters/postgres-tenancy/src/**` on the fly. The CONTEXT packages
do — the suites resolve `@platos/context-secrets` through its package `main`,
which is `dist/` — and the `postgres-tenancy-repository` CI job builds it for
exactly that reason. A cleaned `dist` is the vacuity the classifier exists to
refuse, and it was live on this branch until the job gained its step.
RUN IT ON REAL PostgreSQL. Seven of the eight suites start a container of
their own; an in-memory double cannot falsify a clause whose whole subject is
what the database does with it.

mutations.to:

mutations.note: `FOR UPDATE` is TRANSACTION-scoped.
